MAIUP empirical-FDR pleiotropy screen on a phenotype pair

Source: vignettes/method-maiup.Rmd
method-maiup.Rmd

Function: run_maiup()

Result column: maiup

Family: Pairwise mixture-adjusted IUT

Introduction

Pairwise (traits i,ji,j) Mixture-model-Adjusted Intersection-Union empirical FDR procedure (Zeng et al., MAIUP). It decorrelates the per-trait Z-scores, forms the intersection-union statistic, and calibrates an empirical FDR against a multi-component null mixture (Zeng et al.). MAIUP is run for one trait pair at a time.

Mathematical Framework and Implementation

Decorrelating whitening. Let Z=(Z1,Z2)Z = (Z_1, Z_2) be the per-trait Z-scores. The null cross-trait correlation matrix RR is estimated from variants significant in neither trait (p1≥τp_1 \ge \tau and p2≥τp_2 \ge \tau, with τ\tau = p_threshold). With eigendecomposition R=VΛV⊤R = V \Lambda V^{\top}, the symmetric (ZCA-type) whitening matrix W=VΛ−1/2V⊤W = V \Lambda^{-1/2} V^{\top} produces decorrelated scores Zd=ZWZ^{d} = Z\,W with components Z1d,Z2dZ^{d}_1, Z^{d}_2 and two-sided per-trait p-values

Pkd=2(1−Φ(|Zkd|)),k=1,2. P^{d}_k = 2\,\bigl(1 - \Phi(|Z^{d}_k|)\bigr), \qquad k = 1,2 .

Intersection-union statistic. The IUT statistic for the composite null “associated with at most one trait” is the maximum of the two decorrelated p-values,

Pmax=max⁡(P1d,P2d), P_{\max} = \max\bigl(P^{d}_1, P^{d}_2\bigr),

which rejects only when both traits are individually significant.

Null mixture. Variants fall into four classes by which traits are null: both null (a00a_{00}), only trait 2 non-null (a01a_{01}), only trait 1 non-null (a10a_{10}), and both non-null (the alternative). The null proportions are estimated by Storey-type tail counting at cut c=0.5c = 0.5:

â1=#{P1d≥c}n(1−c),â2=#{P2d≥c}n(1−c),â00=#{P1d≥c,P2d≥c}n(1−c)2, \hat a_{1} = \frac{\#\{P^{d}_1 \ge c\}}{n\,(1-c)}, \quad \hat a_{2} = \frac{\#\{P^{d}_2 \ge c\}}{n\,(1-c)}, \quad \hat a_{00} = \frac{\#\{P^{d}_1 \ge c,\, P^{d}_2 \ge c\}}{n\,(1-c)^2},

followed by â01=max⁡(0,â1−â00)\hat a_{01} = \max(0,\hat a_1 - \hat a_{00}) and â10=max⁡(0,â2−â00)\hat a_{10} = \max(0,\hat a_2 - \hat a_{00}) (with edge corrections, and a one-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov uniformity check that forces âk=1\hat a_k = 1 when a trait’s p-values are indistinguishable from Uniform(0,1)(0,1)).

Marginal null CDFs. For each trait the null CDF of PkdP^{d}_k is estimated nonparametrically by the Least Concave Majorant (LCM) of the empirical CDF, then mixture-adjusted to isolate the null component: F̂k(p)=(FkLCM(p)−akp)/(1−ak)\hat F_k(p) = \bigl(F^{\mathrm{LCM}}_k(p) - a_k\,p\bigr)/(1-a_k).

Empirical FDR. Writing F̂(p)\hat F(p) for the empirical CDF of PmaxP_{\max}, the false-discovery numerator sums the contributions of the three null sub-classes evaluated at p=Pmaxp = P_{\max}:

FDR̂(p)=â01pF̂2(p)+â10pF̂1(p)+â00p2F̂(p). \widehat{\mathrm{FDR}}(p) = \frac{\hat a_{01}\, p\, \hat F_2(p) + \hat a_{10}\, p\, \hat F_1(p) + \hat a_{00}\, p^{2}}{\hat F(p)} .

(Under each sub-null the max-statistic tail factorizes into a uniform factor pp for the null trait and the estimated null CDF for the other, with p2p^2 when both are null.) The returned p_maiup is this FDR after monotone (step-down) enforcement in decreasing PmaxP_{\max} and clamping to [0,1][0,1].

What This Method Advances

MAIUP combines an intersection-union statistic with mixture adjustment, so both traits must show evidence while one-trait null components are modeled explicitly.

Assumptions

  • Cross-trait dependence among null Z-scores is fully captured by the linear correlation RR, so symmetric whitening renders the two traits’ null statistics independent.
  • The genome-wide p-value mixture has the four-class structure above, with each null sub-class contributing a uniform marginal for its null trait(s).
  • LCM/isotonic estimation requires the true null CDF to be concave (p-value density non-increasing), as for well-behaved test statistics.
  • Null proportions are estimable from the upper half (p≥0.5p \ge 0.5) of the p-value distribution (signal sparse near 1).
  • Variants are treated as exchangeable; LD is not explicitly modelled.

When This Method Is a Good Fit

Good for pairwise pleiotropy when empirical FDR calibration and mixture adjustment are desired.

The maiup column is the monotone empirical FDR output returned by the MAIUP implementation, built from the IUT statistic and mixture-adjusted null components.

Pairwise methods use i and j to select the two phenotypes. Re-run the method for each phenotype pair that should be tested.

Minimal Usage 

library(pleioverse)
set.seed(1)
pleio <- run_pleiosim(
  n_phenotype = 3, n_participant = 500,
  n_variant_pleiotropic = 3,
  n_variant_nonpleiotropic = c(3, 3, 3),
  n_variant_null = 30,
  heritability = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
)
pleio <- run_maiup(pleio, i = 1, j = 2)
head(pleio@results$maiup)

Implementation Files

  • R wrapper: R/run_maiup.R
  • C++ kernel or dispatcher: src/maiup.cpp
  • Shared MPAT inputs, where applicable: R/pleiotest.R and src/test_engine.cpp
